name: Brazil
summary: Half of the estate is reserved to the necessary heirs (descendants, ascendants, spouse) and a will cannot touch it (Civil Code arts. 1.846, 1.845). Succession follows the law of the deceased's last domicile, and Brazilian courts alone decide on Brazilian real estate, so a foreign resident cannot opt out. Brazil has no trust law and only charitable-type foundations.
reserved_share: Necessary heirs: descendants, ascendants and spouse (Código Civil art. 1.845). The legítima is one half of the estate (art. 1.846); the other half can be left freely by will.
foreign_law_note: The law of the deceased's last domicile governs succession (LINDB art. 10); for property in Brazil of a foreign deceased, the foreign law applies for the benefit of the Brazilian spouse and children only if it is more favourable to them (art. 10 par. 1). Brazilian courts have exclusive jurisdiction over real estate in Brazil (CPC art. 23). No choice of law by the testator was found.
trust_note: There is no general trust law. The only trust-like device is the fideicomisso, a substitution in a will (Civil Code arts. 1.951-1.960), limited to one generation. Brazil is not a party to the Hague Trusts Convention, and the treatment of foreign trusts is not settled in the sources found. Foundations (Civil Code arts. 62-69) may be created only for religious, moral, cultural or assistance purposes (art. 62 sole paragraph), so a family foundation is not possible.
open_questions: Treatment of foreign trusts by Brazilian courts and the Receita Federal (including ITCMD on trust assets) was not sourced.
Brazilian tax reform and any bill on the legítima or on trusts was not checked.
